name: Daphni
label: Jiaolong
lede: Dan Snaith finished a maths PhD, won a Polaris Prize and started a label so his club tracks had somewhere to go. Daphni is the dancefloor side of Caribou, who was Manitoba until a punk singer threatened to sue.

eras.title: A maths student called Manitoba
eras.text: Before Daphni and Caribou, Dan Snaith was Manitoba, making bedroom electronics for Leaf while he worked toward a doctorate in mathematics. A punk singer's threat to sue ended the name.

years.h: Manitoba's first EP is People Eating Fruit
years.p: [[Dan Snaith|20ffdffa-9e17-4968-98ca-3434064b00bb]] starts releasing music as Manitoba with the EP People Eating Fruit, a year before his first album.

years.h: Start Breaking My Heart sets Manitoba beside Boards of Canada
years.p: Snaith's debut on The Leaf Label gets compared to Boards of Canada, [[Four Tet|3bcff06f-675a-451f-9075-99e8657047e8]] and Aphex Twin.
years.xp:
Pitchfork first scored it 8.0, then revised that to 7.9 in 2006. In 2017 the site put it at No. 40 on its list of the 50 best IDM albums of all time.

It was reissued in 2006 by Domino, after Snaith had become Caribou.

years.h: Up in Flames is the last record to say Manitoba
years.p: Snaith's second album on Leaf is the final one released under that name.

years.src: Wikipedia: Richard Manitoba · Wikipedia: Dan Snaith
years.h: Handsome Dick Manitoba threatens to sue, and Manitoba becomes Caribou
years.p: Richard 'Handsome Dick' Manitoba of the Dictators threatened legal action over the name. Snaith switched to Caribou rather than fight it.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's page on Richard Manitoba puts it in one sentence: in 2004 he threatened to sue Snaith for using the name, and Snaith changed his own to Caribou.

The Manitoba albums were reissued under the new name.

eras.title: Caribou, with a doctorate on the side
eras.text: The new name brings psychedelic pop first and then a record built for the dancefloor. Snaith picks up a PhD, a Polaris Prize and a live band along the way.

years.h: Snaith finishes a maths PhD at Imperial College London
years.p: His doctorate, supervised by Kevin Buzzard, is on overconvergent Siegel modular symbols. His father Victor and his sister Nina are mathematicians too.
years.xp: Snaith has described the thesis himself: 'original, but I would still call it trivial.'

years.big: "Read it off the back of a milk truck"
years.src: Wikipedia: The Milk of Human Kindness
years.h: Caribou's first record gets its name off a truck, he says
years.p: Snaith's own answer, per Wikipedia, on where he found the title of The Milk of Human Kindness. The phrase is Shakespeare's, from Macbeth.
years.xp:
It came out on Leaf and Domino in April 2005, the first record under the Caribou name. Pitchfork gave it 8.5.

Producer Ryan Lewis later sampled 'Subotnick' for a 2009 project with Macklemore.

yt: BBC Collective mini documentary on the Andorra era
years.h: Andorra turns to psychedelic pop
years.p: City Slang releases it in the UK and Merge in the US, with 'Melody Day' as the lead single.
years.xp: Uncut called the lead single the most striking result of Snaith's immersion in psychedelic soft-pop. Pitchfork's Mark Richardson reviewed the record on August 23, 2007.

years.cap: Caribou at the Polaris Music Prize gala, Toronto, 2008
years.h: A record made after a maths doctorate wins the Polaris Prize
years.p: Andorra takes Canada's album-of-the-year prize for 2008.

years.src: Wikipedia: Swim (Caribou album) · The Quietus: Modular Love
years.h: Snaith sifts about 700 tracks down to nine for Swim
years.p: He says he simply got up each day wanting to make music. Nights DJing at London's Plastic People pushed the result toward the dancefloor.
years.xp:
Nights DJing at London's Plastic People pushed him toward the dancefloor. Snaith told The Quietus he saw Theo Parrish play there and made 'Bowls' within days; he was already thinking about Daphni, he said, because 'there was stuff that needed another outlet.'

Pitchfork gave Swim 8.4 and later put it on its 2014 list of the 100 best albums of the decade so far. Resident Advisor named it album of 2010. 'Odessa' turned up in FIFA 11 and in ads for Lexus and Tissot.

eras.title: Daphni gets a label
eras.text: Daphni takes the tracks that don't fit a Caribou record: quick, loop-based, made for the next DJ set. They go out on Snaith's own Jiaolong label while the Caribou band keeps touring.

years.src: Various Small Flames: Four Tet/Daphni · Wikipedia: Daphni (musician)
years.h: Daphni debuts on a 12-inch shared with Four Tet
years.p: 'Ye Ye' is on [[Four Tet|3bcff06f-675a-451f-9075-99e8657047e8]]'s Text label, with Kieran Hebden taking the flip with 'Pinnacles'.
years.xp:
Various Small Flames called Daphni another pseudonym of Caribou's Dan Snaith.

The same month came Daphni Edits Vol. 1 on Resista, followed by Vol. 2 in August.

years.h: JIAOLONG001 starts a label with as little fuss as possible
years.p: It is Daphni's first 12-inch on Jiaolong, the label Snaith set up in October 2011.
years.xp:
XLR8R reports he built the label so tracks could arrive and disappear from shops the way dance records do.

'Daphni' is Greek for bay leaf. Snaith picked it for its femininity and organic quality, per the same piece.

years.src: The Quietus: Modular Love · XLR8R: Deep Inside: Daphni 'Jiaolong' · Wikipedia: Jiaolong (album)
yt: Daphni Boiler Room London DJ set
years.h: Jiaolong is nine tracks, five of them older singles
years.p: The first Daphni album adds four new tracks to five earlier singles, most made on a modular synth Snaith built himself.
years.xp:
'Each of the tracks on the record was made in a day,' Snaith told The Quietus. He says the modular 'doesn't allow you the possibility of going back and second guessing yourself.'

Metacritic collected 76; NME and Spin each gave it 8/10. It made the 2013 Polaris longlist.

years.cap: Dan Snaith of Caribou opening for Radiohead, Tinley Park, Illinois, June 2012
q: The whole idea is it's not just me, and it's not just hired guns.
years.h: Caribou opens for Radiohead on the King of Limbs tour
years.p: Snaith's live band, with Ryan Smith, Brad Weber and later John Schmersal, plays support dates.
years.xp:
Snaith says the live show is its own thing, a proper band in which everyone is equally part of it.

Smith has played with him since 2003, Weber since 2007 and Schmersal since 2009.

years.h: Owen Pallett is credited on the Julia / Tiberius 12-inch
years.p: The Daphni single comes out on Jiaolong in April 2014 with [[Owen Pallett|6d394418-a565-4c16-9dec-f5a89e213cde]] credited.

years.src: Wikipedia: Our Love (Caribou album) · Wikipedia: Dan Snaith
years.h: Snaith writes Our Love after his daughter's birth
years.p: A more personal record, with [[Jessy Lanza|0dfb3c3d-e140-4575-baf3-7ff20ae56c9c]] and Owen Pallett on some tracks. Pitchfork tags it Best New Music.
years.xp:
City Slang released it, with Merge following the next day.

It was nominated for a Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album, made the 2015 Polaris shortlist and won the IMPALA Album of the Year award.

eras.title: A Fabric mix, a second album, a voice up front
eras.text: Daphni gets a proper DJ mix and a second album, and Snaith puts his own voice at the front of the next Caribou record.

years.h: FabricLive.93 packs 27 tracks into 73 minutes
years.p: Snaith's Fabric mix, released as Daphni, includes Luther Davis Group, Pheeroan akLaff and Container.

years.h: Joli Mai is the second Daphni album
years.p: Twelve tracks and 59 minutes on his own Jiaolong label, some drawn from the Fabric mix.
years.xp:
Metacritic collected 78.

It placed No. 10 on Exclaim!'s 2017 dance/electronic list and No. 5 on Rolling Stone's 20 best EDM/electronic albums of 2017.

years.h: A Daphni EP called Sizzling
years.p: Out in June 2019, with a title track that also came out as a single.

years.cap: Caribou at the 9:30 Club, Washington, DC
years.h: Snaith whittles 900 ideas down to 12 tracks for Suddenly
years.p: He names it after a word his daughter was obsessed with. Pitchfork gave it 8.2.
years.xp:
It won the 2021 Juno for Electronic Album of the Year and made the Polaris shortlist.

The singles were 'Home', 'You and I' and 'Never Come Back'.

eras.title: Cherry
eras.text: Five years after Joli Mai, the third Daphni album arrives. Pitchfork scores it 8.2 and ranks it No. 25 of 2022.

years.src: Resident Advisor: Daphni - Cherry · Consequence: Caribou's Dan Snaith announces new Daphni album Cherry
years.h: Three singles lead in, starting with 'Cherry'
years.p: Resident Advisor describes the title track as a DX7 and a bassline that spirals out. 'Cloudy' follows in June with the album announcement, and 'Mania' joins them.
years.xp: Resident Advisor's single review heard a three-note motif mid-track bent and warmed-over like the melodies on old Manitoba records. Snaith called the essence of 'Cloudy' keeping it aloft, like nudging a balloon that's only just heavier than air.

q: The most fun there is to be had on a dance record this year.
years.src: Wikipedia: Cherry (Daphni album) · Album of the Year: Daphni - Cherry
years.h: Pitchfork gives Cherry 8.2 and ranks it No. 25 of 2022
years.p: Fourteen tracks and 47 minutes, recorded at Metropolis Studio in London and released on Jiaolong.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Sherburne called it 'a tour de force of dancefloor intuition and emotional release.' Metacritic gave it 82 from eight reviews; AllMusic picked it among its electronic albums of the year, and The Atlantic ranked it No. 4 of 2022. Matt Colton mastered it.

eras.title: Back to Caribou, then back to Daphni
eras.text: A big dancefloor Caribou record comes first. A fourth Daphni album follows and makes the Polaris longlist.

yt: Boiler Room Belfast, the Honey live debut
years.h: Honey brings Caribou to the dancefloor, loud
years.p: 'Volume' samples MARRS' 'Pump Up the Volume'. Pitchfork gave the record 7.8, Metacritic 73.
years.xp: Snaith said he wanted 'huge dancefloor tracks' and to keep the thrill when something hits really hard. It made the 2025 Polaris longlist.

years.h: Butterfly, the fourth Daphni album, makes the Polaris longlist
years.p: Wikipedia also lists an expanded edition with seven new tracks and remixes for September 2026.
